Neither is rewarded, which is the point of subtracting 2/(K_eff+1).

const answer = `METRIC: hfsc_rank_l1
TITLE: Hyperbolic free-energy cell rank: chance-corrected soft rank of the true level-1 cell under a leave-one-out Karcher barycentre of the full training history, scored against the whole per-cell negative distribution.
FORMULA:
Ball B^d = {x in R^d : ||x|| < 1} with constant curvature c = -1, Riemannian distance
  d(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2c^{-1} ... ) -- implemented concretely as
  d(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2*||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)*(1-||y||^2)) )   [arcosh of the standard Poincare-ball formula, c = -1]
Karcher/Frechet mean of a finite set S in (B,d): the point m minimising sum_{y in S} d(m,y)^2, computed by Riemannian gradient descent with step 1, initialised at the Euclidean mean of S projected into the ball by x -> x*(1-1e-6)/max(1,||x||), run to ||grad|| < 1e-8 or 30 iterations, whichever first (no tuned constant: step 1 and tolerance 30 are fixed a priori, not fitted).
beta = 1/tau_ref, where tau_ref is the contrastive temperature stored in the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (its learned inverse-temperature scale if that is the stored form).
For a training pair (q,p): H_q = { j : (q,j) in TRAIN }. Drop p: H_q^- = H_q \\ {p}; m_q = KarcherMean({ u_j : j in H_q^- }) if H_q^- is non-empty, else m_q = u_q, where u_j is the reference's SOURCE representation of item j.
For every item i != q let delta_i = d(m_q, v_i), where v_i is the reference's TARGET representation of item i.
For every level-1 cell c with member set C_c = { i : code1(i) = c }, let C_c^- = C_c \\ {q} and
  F_c = -(1/beta) * log( (1/|C_c^-|) * sum_{i in C_c^-} exp(-beta * delta_i) )     (the per-item free energy = size-neutral log-mean-exp soft minimum; empty C_c^- cells are dropped)
K_eff = number of cells with C_c^- non-empty. c_p = code1(p). With sigma(z) = 1/(1+exp(-z)):
  pi_q = 1 + sum_{c != c_p} sigma( beta * (F_{c_p} - F_c) )
  r_q  = 1 / pi_q
M = (1/|TRAIN|) * sum_{(q,p) in TRAIN} r_q  -  2/(K_eff + 1)
Higher is better. The subtracted term is the exact chance level: it equals 1/pi for the all-cells-tied configuration, so a table that carries no cell information scores 0 and a one-code table (K_eff = 1) scores exactly 0.
INPUTS: (1) the exported SID table - the level-1 integer code per item only (levels 2..L are read but unused); (2) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference - per-item source representation u_i and target representation v_i, plus its stored contrastive temperature tau_ref; (3) the TRAINING split, used only for the pair list and for building H_q. Nothing else; no validation pair, no test pair, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
GEOMETRY: curvature enters (i) in d, which is the Poincare-ball Riemannian distance at c = -1, not a Euclidean distance: it diverges as either argument approaches the boundary, so cells whose members sit near the sphere are penalised much more than their Euclidean offset suggests; (ii) in the Karcher mean m_q, which is the Riemannian barycentre of the history's source points - the arithmetic mean of the same points lies off the geodesic and is a different point of the ball, so the query location itself is curvature-dependent; (iii) in the free energy F_c, which is a log-partition function of the per-item distance distribution, i.e. a soft minimum of the full negative population. Curvature is fixed at c = -1 exactly (nothing is tuned); beta = 1/tau_ref is inherited from the reference, not fitted.
WHY IT SHOULD TRACK RECALL: Stage 3 walks the code tree and can only re-rank the ten items that its beam reaches, so recall is capped by whether the true item's level-1 cell is reachable for the query. This metric measures exactly that reachability with the reference as the arbiter: it asks, for each training query, which cell contains the item that the reference's geodesic geometry says is nearest to the query's whole training history, and where the true cell sits in that soft ordering. It adds three things over Q_H and over HBAA. First, it keeps HBAA's full-history barycentre but replaces the mean of ten negatives with the free energy of the entire per-cell negative population, so a cell that hides one negative almost exactly on the query is penalised instead of being averaged away - and the Stage-3 re-rank is precisely a competition against the single best negative, not against an average. Second, it is an order statistic over the item distribution, so it is sensitive to the shape (the left tail) of the negative distribution, which the mean cannot see; this is the one information source the brief identifies as still unused. Third, its collapse behaviour is analytic: the K_eff chance offset and the |C_c|^-1 normalisation make the one-code, few-code and relabelled tables score 0 rather than high, which is what sank the plain path likelihood (-0.488) and its canonical collapse reward.
COMPUTE: one Karcher mean per training pair over |H_q|-1 history points (|H| * 30 * d flops, negligible) plus one distance vector over N = 24587 items (24587 * d flops) and one segmented log-mean-exp over the 256 cells. The distance vectors are the cost: they are formed as a chunked GEMM (chunk x d) @ (d x 24587) with the precomputed ||v_i||^2 and then arcosh, so |TRAIN| = 1e4 pairs, d = 64 is about 1.6e10 flops, roughly 10-20 s on BLAS; 5e4 pairs is about 50-60 s. Memory is one 24587-vector of floats per query plus the 24587 x 64 representation matrix (~6 MB), all in float32/float64 dense arrays. Well under a minute for any plausible training split, and level-1 only means K_eff <= 256 and the cell reduction is O(N) per query.
RISKS: (i) if the reference's candidate set is not the full item catalogue, the free energy is over a different population than the one Stage 3 ranks, which flattens the signal; (ii) if the reference stores only a learned inverse temperature without a temperature, beta must fall back to beta = 1 (curvature-normalised units), which changes the sharpness of the soft minimum while leaving the ranking argument intact - the chance offset is unaffected because it does not contain beta; (iii) the segmentation assumes code1 is the exported level-1 column and that padding/duplicate sentinel codes are excluded, otherwise empty sentinel cells enter K_eff and inflate the subtraction; (iv) if a query's history is a singleton the fallback m_q = u_q reintroduces a direct source-target comparison for that pair, which is noisier than the barycentre but is bounded by one pair; (v) with very skewed reference norms, d saturates (arcosh of a huge argument), many cells tie in F_c and M is driven toward 0, i.e. toward the chance level rather than to a false positive; (vi) it shares HBAA's dependence on the reference's source/target alignment, so if the reference is weak this inherits that weakness.
FAILURE MODE: worst on a HUB-AND-SPOKE level-1 table, where each of the K cells contains one geodesically central medoid item plus uniformly random remaining items. The medoid pins every cell's free energy to nearly the same value, so F_{c_p} - F_c is near 0 for all c on every pair, the sigmoids sit at 1/2, pi_q -> (K_eff+1)/2 and M -> 0 (and slightly negative where the true cell's medoid happens to be the worst). Second worst on extreme size skew - one very large cell plus 255 singletons - because the large cell wins the soft minimum for every query and all true singleton cells accumulate exceedance, pushing M below 0. In both cases the table has thrown away the information that would let a prefix-restricted beam reach the right items, and the metric correctly reports no value rather than rewarding the collapse.
END METRIC`;

await tools.progress.append_progress({ content: "STAGE 6 - FINAL ANSWER RECORD (complete, self-contained).\n\n" + answer });
return "appended final answer record";

First, it keeps HBAA's full-history barycentre but replaces the mean over ten negative barycentres with the free energy of the entire per-cell negative population, so a cell hiding one negative almost exactly on the query is penalised instead of having it averaged away — and the Stage-3 re-rank is exactly a competition against the single best negative, not against an average. Second, it is an order statistic over the item distribution and therefore sensitive to the left tail of the negatives, the one information source the brief identifies as still unused; a mean cannot see that tail. Third, its collapse behaviour is analytic rather than empirical: the K_eff chance offset plus the 1/|C_c^-| normalisation forces one-code, few-code and relabelled tables to 0, which is precisely what sank plain path likelihood (-0.488) and its collapse reward, and it does so without any size-matched shuffling null (whose bad construction already showed up as +0.061 in hbaa_size_matched_kept).
COMPUTE: one Karcher mean per training pair over |H_q|-1 history points (|H|·30·d flops, negligible), plus one distance vector over N = 24587 items (24587·d flops) and one segmented log-mean-exp over 256 cells. The distance vectors dominate and are formed as a chunked GEMM (chunk x d) @ (d x 24587) against precomputed ||v_i||^2, followed by arcosh: 1e4 pairs at d = 64 is about 1.6e10 flops, roughly 10-20 s on BLAS; 5e4 pairs is about 50-60 s. Memory is one 24587-vector per query plus the 24587 x 64 representation matrix (~6 MB), all dense float arrays. Because only level 1 is used, K_eff <= 256 and the cell reduction is O(N) per query, so the whole thing finishes inside a minute on 24587 items.
RISKS: (i) if the reference's candidate set is narrower than the full catalogue, the free energy is taken over a different population than Stage 3 ranks, which flattens the signal; (ii) if the reference exposes only a learned inverse temperature and not a temperature, beta falls back to beta = 1 in curvature-normalised units — this changes the sharpness of the soft minimum but not the ranking argument, and the chance offset is unaffected because it contains no beta; (iii) the segmentation assumes code1 is the exported level-1 column and that padding/duplicate sentinel codes are excluded, otherwise empty sentinel cells enter K_eff and inflate the subtraction; (iv) a singleton history falls back to m_q = u_q, reintroducing a direct source-target comparison for that one pair (bounded, but noisier); (v) with very skewed reference norms, d saturates, many cells tie in F_c and M is driven to the chance level 0 rather than to a false positive; (vi) it shares HBAA's dependence on the reference's source/target alignment, so a weak reference weakens it too.
FAILURE MODE: worst on a HUB-AND-SPOKE level-1 table, where each of the K cells holds one geodesically central medoid item plus uniformly random remaining items. The medoid pins every cell's free energy to nearly the same value, so F_{c_p} - F_c is near 0 on every pair, the sigmoids sit at 1/2, pi_q tends to (K_eff+1)/2 and M tends to 0 (slightly negative where the true cell's medoid happens to be the furthest). Second worst on extreme size skew — one very large cell plus 255 singletons — because the large cell wins the soft minimum for every query, true singleton cells accumulate exceedance, and M goes below 0. In both cases the table has thrown away the information that would let a prefix-restricted beam reach the right items, and the metric correctly reports no value instead of rewarding the collapse.
END METRIC
